## Norm

:::{.definition data-title="Norm"}

For a [[vector-spaces|vector space]] $V$ over $\mathbb{R}$, a
**norm** is a function $\lVert\cdot\rVert:V\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfying, for all
$v,w\in V$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$:

1. $\lVert v\rVert\geq0$;
2. $\lVert v\rVert=0$ if and only if $v=0$;
3. $\lVert\alpha v\rVert=\lvert\alpha\rvert\lVert v\rVert$ (homogeneity);
4. $\lVert v+w\rVert\leq\lVert v\rVert+\lVert w\rVert$ (triangle inequality).

:::

## Normed Space

:::{.definition data-title="Normed Space"}

The pair $(V,\lVert\cdot\rVert)$ of a vector space and a norm is a **normed
space**. A **Banach space** is a normed space that is complete, that is, every
Cauchy sequence converges (see [[metric-spaces]]).

:::

:::{.theorem data-title="Norms Induce Metrics"}

If $\lVert\cdot\rVert$ is a norm on $V$ then $d(v,w):=\lVert v-w\rVert$ is a
metric on $V$.

:::

:::{.proof}
Positivity and $d(v,w)=0\iff v=w$ follow from norm axioms 1 and 2. Symmetry
follows from axiom 3 with $\alpha=-1$. The triangle inequality for $d$ follows
from axiom 4 applied to $v-u=(v-w)+(w-u)$.
:::

## Examples

- $\mathbb{R}^n$ with the $p$-norm $\lVert x\rVert_p=\left(\sum_i\lvert x_i\rvert^p\right)^{1/p}$
  for $p\geq1$, see [[lp-norm]].
- $C([0,1])$ with the sup norm $\lVert f\rVert_\infty=\sup_{x}\lvert f(x)\rvert$,
  which is a Banach space, and with the integral norm
  $\lVert f\rVert_1=\int_0^1\lvert f\rvert$, which is not complete.

An [[inner-product-space|inner product]] always induces a norm
$\lVert v\rVert=\sqrt{\langle v,v\rangle}$; a complete inner product space is a
[[hilbert-spaces|Hilbert space]].
